**RE: Member Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
*   **Patient Name:** Taylor Jennings
*   **Member ID:** W164265496
*   **Plan:** 'Ohana Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Hawaii
*   **Reference Number:** POC-209DEB4204-66822
*   **Requested Service:** Total Shoulder Replacement (CPT Code 23472)
*   **Ordering Surgeon:** Dr. Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Department,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), scheduled with Dr. Okafor, MD. The denial letter dated August 15, 2026, states that the "clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." 

This determination is clinically and factually incorrect under your plan's governing medical policy, **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769 for Shoulder Arthroplasty (Effective July 2025)**. The clinical records submitted with the initial authorization request demonstrate that I not only completed an extensive trial of conservative treatment that far exceeds your policy's requirements, but I also meet the explicit criteria that exempts me from needing a conservative trial altogether.

### 1. Proof of Exhaustive Non-Operative/Conservative Treatment

Your policy, Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769, states that medically necessary total shoulder arthroplasty requires:
> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment that includes at least ONE of the following:
> * Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program
> * Rest or activity modification
> * Application of heat or ice
> * Pharmacologic treatment (oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics)
> * Corticosteroid injections"

My clinical records document extensive failure of multiple modalities listed above:
*   **Supervised Physical Therapy:** I completed **16 weeks** of formal, supervised physical therapy (from March 8, 2026, to June 28, 2026) totaling **24 visits**. This program focused heavily on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, as documented in my attached physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds your 12-week requirement by a full month.
*   **Pharmacologic Treatment:** I have taken oral NSAIDs for **6 months** with completely inadequate pain relief.
*   **Corticosteroid Injections:** I received an intra-articular corticosteroid injection on **May 12, 2026**, which provided only 4 weeks of partial relief before my severe symptoms returned.

### 2. Immediate Clinical Exception to Non-Operative Treatment

Furthermore, Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769 contains an explicit clinical exception regarding radiographic findings of end-stage joint disease. The policy states:
> "Complete or near-complete loss of joint space* on axillary or AP X-rays (internal rotation and/or external rotation)*"
> 
> "*NOTE: In those with bone-on-bone articulation on axillary or true AP X-rays, non-operative treatment is not required"

My shoulder radiographs dated **July 14, 2026** (true AP and axillary views) reveal **complete loss of glenohumeral joint space**, along with severe osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. This complete loss of joint space represents a bone-on-bone articulation. According to your own policy, my non-operative conservative treatment trial was not even contractually required to approve this surgery, though I completed a 16-week trial anyway.

### 3. Fulfillment of All Other Clinical Criteria under Guideline 1769

My clinical records show complete alignment with all other criteria within Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769:
*   **"Evidence of painful osteoarthritis or inflammatory, non-infectious arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid) with functional limitations such as ADLs, employment, or recreation":** I have suffered from 14 months of progressive, severe shoulder pain that is completely unrelieved by rest. Functionally, I cannot reach overhead, dress myself without assistance, or sleep on my affected side. My physical exam reveals severe glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees.
*   **"Functional and intact rotator cuff and deltoid (adequate abduction strength); confirmed by physical examination, MRI, or CT scan":** Physical examination confirms my rotator cuff strength is intact, and a shoulder CT scan performed on **July 14, 2026**, objectively confirms an intact rotator cuff.
*   **"No cortisone injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery":** My only corticosteroid injection was administered on **May 12, 2026**. This is well outside the restricted 12-week pre-operative window.
*   **"No prior arthroscopic surgery of the shoulder within 12 weeks of surgery":** I have had no prior arthroscopic shoulder surgeries.
*   **General Requirements:** I have no active infections, no untreated substance use issues, a healthy BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker, making me fully optimized for elective joint surgery.

### Conclusion

I have met and exceeded every clinical metric required for Total Shoulder Arthroplasty under 'Ohana Health Plan's guidelines. I have completed 16 weeks of physical therapy and 6 months of NSAID therapy, and my July 14, 2026, X-rays show end-stage bone-on-bone joint destruction, which waives the conservative care requirement entirely.

Please review the attached physical therapy discharge notes, radiographic reports, CT scan report, and Dr. Okafor's clinical visit notes. I request an immediate reversal of this denial so that I may proceed with this medically necessary procedure to restore my basic quality of life and physical function.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent matter.

Sincerely,

Taylor Jennings
